# SK4003 — Review a temporary params array with a span overload

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

An explicit temporary array passed to a params parameter has an accessible ReadOnlySpan overload.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Performance |
| Default severity | hint |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | 12.0 |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

A span-based call may avoid the temporary array. The analyzer speculatively binds an explicit ReadOnlySpan collection expression and verifies an accessible matching overload; it does not assume two overload bodies have identical semantics.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
Consume(new int[] { 1, 2, 3 }); // Both params int[] and ReadOnlySpan<int> overloads exist.
```

Write:

```csharp
Consume((System.ReadOnlySpan<int>)[1, 2, 3]); // After reviewing the overload's behavior.
```

## When it does not fire

Only nonempty explicit/implicit array creations with initializers passed as the last argument to a params array parameter are reported. Requires C# 12 and an accessible same-type overload with matching preceding parameter types/ref kinds, return type and a ReadOnlySpan of the same element type. Existing arrays, empty allocations, named/omitted arguments, dynamic calls, expression trees, await elements, pointer element types and missing or inaccessible alternatives are excluded. Expanded params calls and declaration changes belong outside this initial call-site rule. Report-only because overload semantics and actual allocation elimination require review.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK4003.severity`
